 Why 150K inactive Louisiana voter registrations could be canceled — and why the number grew 
 BY ALYSE PFEIL | Staff writer 
 Alyse Pfeil

 Louisiana could cancel roughly 150,000 inactive voter registrations if those residents don’t cast ballots in the November election .
 That number could be dramatically higher than in previous years because the Legislature recently tightened procedures for keeping the state’s voter rolls up to date, leading to more registrations being designated inactive.
 State leaders argue the new system ensures only qualified voters cast a ballot.
 “Accurate voter rolls are essential to fair and secure elections and are required by state and federal law,” Secretary of State spokesperson Trey Williams said in a statement. “Our goal is not to remove eligible voters from the rolls. Our goal is to ensure our voter registration records are accurate and up to date.”
 But voting rights advocates worry the changes could disenfranchise people.
 “We often hear people saying that they choose to sit out the vote,” said M. Christian Green, president of the League of Women Voters of Louisiana. “But that choice has a consequence, and they could find out that, when they do want to exercise their right to vote, they don’t have that opportunity because they’re no longer on the rolls.”
 How it works
 If someone is listed as inactive in the state's voter rolls for two federal elections, their registration gets canceled. Inactive voters are identified by the state’s annual canvass.
 In Louisiana, before 2025, election officials used U.S. Postal Service records to review registration information and flag voters who appeared to have moved. Voters would be labeled inactive when the registrar of voters received information indicating that someone had moved or was no longer qualified to vote.
 In 2025, Louisiana started an additional review: Registered voters who have not voted or updated their registration in the last 10 years can now automatically be designated as inactive.
 Data from the Secretary of State shows the number of inactive registrations has jumped under the expanded voter roll canvass.
 As of August 2026, there were 447,000 inactive voters, and in 2025 there were 456,000 inactive voters.
 In 2024, before the expanded canvass took effect, Louisiana had about 319,000 inactive voters; in 2023 that figure was 229,000, in 2022 it was 182,000 and in 2020 it was 150,000.
 About 87,000 inactive voter registrations were canceled after the 2024 election. After the 2022 election, that number was about 53,000; after the 2020 election it was 49,000; after 2018 it was 45,000; and after 2016 it was 57,000, data from the Secretary of State’s Office shows.
 What does it mean?
 Rep. Les Farnum, R-Sulphur, who sponsored legislation in 2024 that expanded the canvass, did not respond to a request for comment. But during a public hearing on the bill that year, he said the more extensive voter list checks were aimed at ensuring Louisiana has “good, clean” voter registration lists.
 “I absolutely do not view this as voter suppression,” Farnum said. “It’s about accuracy in your voting rolls.”
 But voting advocates say the stringent procedures raise questions about access to the ballot.
 ACLU of Louisiana Advocacy Director Sarah Whittington said ensuring voters rolls are accurate “is an entirely noble and democratic undertaking,” but she questioned whether the new canvass process is designed more to benefit election officials or actual voters.
 Green shares that skepticism.
 “We really have the sense that most of the public doesn’t understand that voting is a right that can be taken away,” Green said.
 Green said the League of Women Voters supports effective voter list maintenance and believes that only living, eligible U.S. citizen voters should be on the rolls.
 But she said problems arise when eligible registered voters “are being swept into voter purges unaware.”
 Williams, the Secretary of State spokesperson, contends voters have ample time and notice to check their registration status and update it if need be, and he said the expanded voter roll checks help officials identify outdated registration records, including people who have moved out of state or died.
 “Inactive voters have two regularly scheduled federal elections to verify their information and return to the active voter list, or up to 14 years total,” Williams said. “Louisiana law includes safeguards to protect eligible voters throughout the voter roll maintenance process, including sending an address confirmation card.”
 Check your voter registration
 Early voting runs until Oct. 27, excluding Sunday, and Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 Inactive voters are still registered to vote and are often eligible to cast a ballot. Since Louisiana’s registration deadline has passed, inactive voters can go to their polling place to update their information and vote.
 “When a voter is placed on the inactive list, they are still eligible to vote, and it does not take that right away,” Williams said.
 Inactive voters whose address hasn’t changed must simply attest in writing at their polling place that the listed address is correct. Inactive voters who have moved inside the same parish or moved to a new parish within the last three months must list their updated address. Inactive voters who have permanently moved out of Louisiana are ineligible to vote.
 Voters can check their registration online at voterportal.sos.la.gov/inactivevoters or using the Secretary of State’s GeauxVote app, or by calling the registrar of voters in their parish.
